simple.meaning: מְדִינָה (mᵉdîynâh) appears 53 times in the Hebrew Scriptures and is introduced in connection with kingship and in connection with priesthood.
simple.biblicalBackground: The first appearances are in 1 Kings, Ezra, Nehemiah, Esther, Ecclesiastes, and 3 more, beginning at 1 Kings 20:14. BibleIQ detects the main surrounding context as kingship, priesthood, city, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מְדִינָה (H4082) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: People in Scripture are understood by their place in the story. BibleIQ follows מְדִינָה through the actual verses so the reader sees the person in context instead of as an isolated dictionary entry.
simple.summary: מְדִינָה (mᵉdîynâh) / H4082 is tracked through 1 Kings 20:14, 1 Kings 20:15, 1 Kings 20:17, 1 Kings 20:19. The entry is generated from source alignment, occurrence evidence, and the surrounding Scripture context.

definitions.short: properly, a judgeship , i.e. jurisdiction ; by implication, a district (as ruled by a judge); generally, a region
definitions.full: H4082. medinah מְדִינָה noun feminine province (an Aramaic word, compare Syriac , Arabic city ) **compare also Old Aramaic מדינתא city , Palmyrene מדיתא city , suffix מדיתהון , plural מדינתא SAC 70 Lzb 306 Cooke 266 . — Est 1:1 28t.; plural מְדִינוֺת 1Kin 20:14 23 t.; — a district of an empire, 1 districts of realm of Ahab with שׂרים over them 1Kin 20:14-15 , 17 , 19 . 2 of the Babylonian empire : Ezek 19:8 ; Dan 8:2 (of Elam); בַּמְּדִינוֺת שָׂרָתִי princess among the provinces Lam 1:1 (of Judea). 3 of the Persian empire Est 1:1 + often; one of which was Palestine, Neh 1:3 ; the returning exiles, הַמְּדִינָה בְּנֵי children of the province Ezra 2:1 ; Neh 7:6 having הַמְּדִינָה רָאשֵׁי 11:3 . 4 provinces in General Eccl 2:8 ; 5:7 ; מְדִינָה בְּמִשְׁמַנֵּי in the fat places of the province Dan 11:24 (fertile regions, probably Egypt; other translations see in Bev.)
